findings.what: From a slip of 1.00 Ω up to about 1.10 Ω at the opening 0.02 Ω, the line under the picture says 'One slipped reading stretches the bracket far past the honest swarm'. But the bracket is still inside the honest swarm: 0.770 to 0.840 Ω at 1.00, against honest readings from 0.76 to 0.85 Ω. It only passes both ends from about 1.10 Ω, and is far past them only from about 1.3 Ω. Choose the sentence by whether mean ± SD actually passes the honest readings' ends, with a plain 'The slip stretches the bracket' below that.

findings.where: Steps 3 'A slipped probe' and 10 'Back to the fifty', the fade while the probe has slipped
findings.what: The fade is measured against an SD the slip has inflated. So the honest swarm goes pale: at 1.80 Ω a bead at 0.76 Ω goes from z −1.97 to −0.42, and the 0.80 Ω column turns from blue to orange. Nothing on screen says why, and on step 3 the SD has not been taught. On step 10 one sentence could make it a lesson: 'The colours pale too. They measure distance in SDs, and the SD has grown.'

findings.where: Shared B.fade (z = 0 takes cat1); seen on 'Where it balances', 'Same range', 'Work it out' and 'Bumpy or flat' once answered
findings.what: A bead exactly on the mean takes pale cat1, the key's 'higher' colour. This lesson's puzzles put beads right on the mean: Set A's three at 0.80 Ω, the bumpy set's four, the 0.80 Ω bead in 'Work it out', and the 0.81 Ω bead once 'Where it balances' is answered. So they read as slightly above it. Give z = 0 the neutral faintest mix. This fix belongs in dataviz.md, so all five lessons get it.

findings.where: Step 6 'Halve the random error' at 0.01 Ω (paintVals, va = FA.v)
findings.what: At 0.01 Ω the taller swarm leaves no room under the pegs. So the mean's dashed line fades out along with its value, just as the after-text says the balance stays at very nearly 0.80 Ω. Keep the dashed line up to the swarm's top and drop only the value.

findings.where: Step 1 'Fifty readings', finished picture (still traces the ringed bead)
findings.what: The still picture draws one bead's path, and that hides the mean's dashed line and value. So on screen 1, in reduced motion and on return, the mean is never marked, although the text names it. Leave the trace out of the still, or keep the mean marked beside it.

findings.where: Step 12 'One circuit or ten', R.sdA / R.mB / R.sdB in paintTwo
findings.what: The three tiles show their final 0.020, 0.620 and 0.130 Ω from the first frame. But the beads are still dropping, and the fulcrums only slide in at 2.7 s. The guide says that while beads land, the tiles give what is drawn now.

findings.where: Step 5 'Spread by a factor', the Scale choice (#ctl)
findings.what: The 'By factors | Even' choice re-sorts the beads, but it sits under the drawing with the sliders. The guide puts a choice that re-sorts above the drawing.
The pour and rise make their last change at 5.11 s on the film. That is just past the 5 s budget; trim the slow start or the rise wave a little.
'At a random error of 0.02 Ω the SD comes out close to 0.02 Ω, and at 0.01 Ω close to 0.01 Ω.' is 23 words. Split it in two.
The explain text still says 'So the pile grows nearly twice as tall' and 'Yet the pile balances in very nearly the same place'. The screens show a swarm, so these should say 'swarm'.
The step control's max is 12, but the lesson has fourteen screens (0 to 13), as its own whatAmILookingAt and the stepper say. i5 uses 13.

The films show the whole page, 26 frames each, so a frame is about 85 px wide on the sheet. The pour, the rise, the colour welling up and the values' arrival cannot be judged from them. Film the drawing alone (--crop "svg.bd-scene"), as the guide says, before the next review.
